sourcedFrom: BANISH 46-V2 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED (NOT PRINTED)
cleanIntro: An 8 inch, 15.3 oz titanium can with a stainless blast baffle, built on an industry standard HUB mount and rated across an unusually wide span — 5.56 up to .460. Twelve baffles inside: eleven indexed plus one accuracy baffle. ⛔ Its end cap torque is 40 in-lbs, a third of the 110-120 in-lbs every other Banish rifle can uses, and that figure must never be carried across. The manual's cover reads BANISH 46-V2; its own installation section calls the product the BANISH 46.

steps.title: Clear the host, using the host's own manual
steps.action: Unload the firearm and open the action so the chamber is visibly clear before the can is touched. Banish gives no clearing sequence — it sends you to your firearm's own manual, which on a can spanning 5.56 to .460 is the only workable answer.
steps.prose: That span is the point: this can legitimately lives on a semi-auto rifle one week and a big-bore lever gun the next, and they do not clear alike.
steps.quote: If you are at all unsure as to the proper procedures to ensure that your firearm is unloaded, please consult your firearm user’s manual/instructions and/or contact a properly licensed dealer or the manufacturer of your firearm.
steps.cite: BANISH 46-V2 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: The host firearm's manual is the clearing authority.

steps.title: Banish 46 range — 5.56 to .460
steps.action: Match the host to the rating. The SPECS block gives CALIBER .460 and CALIBER RANGE 5.56 - .460, with LIMITED full-auto rating and a stainless steel blast baffle in a titanium body. That upper figure is what makes this can unusual and it is also the reason its end cap torque is different from every other Banish rifle can.
steps.prose: At 15.3 oz it is the heaviest can in the Banish rifle line, and the mass is where the .460 rating comes from.
steps.quote: All Banish suppressors have been designed for unmatched sound suppression. Testing shows that the Banish 46-V2 has an average, at ear, sound reduction of 30db.
steps.cite: BANISH 46-V2 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — SPECS, p.3

steps.title: ⛔ The mount goes into the can first, at 50-60 in-lbs
steps.action: This is a HUB can, so before it ever meets a barrel the supplied mount has to be threaded into the suppressor and tightened to 50 to 60 in-lbs. A HUB can with a loose or absent mount will still physically go onto a host and will be dangerously off axis.
steps.prose: Note the two different torques on this can: 50-60 in-lbs for the mount into the body, and only 40 in-lbs for the end cap. They are not interchangeable numbers.
steps.quote: Prior to mounting the suppressor to the firearm you must first thread and tighten the mount (shipped with the suppressor) into the suppressor. Carefully thread the mount into the suppressor and tighten to 50-60 in-lbs.
steps.cite: BANISH 46-V2 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — INSTALLATION OF MOUNT INTO SUPPRESSOR, p.4
steps.warn: Mount to body: 50-60 in-lbs. End cap: 40 in-lbs. Different joints, different figures.

steps.title: A Nielson device is a separate build inside the mount
steps.action: If you bought a Nielson device mounting interface — the booster a tilting-barrel pistol host needs — it has to be assembled into the suppressor mount as well: piston with the spring over it into the mount, then locked down with the piston cap. That is a second sub-assembly inside the mount, not an accessory that clips on.
steps.prose: On a rifle host you will never touch this. On a pistol host it is the part that lets the slide cycle at all.
steps.quote: If you purchased a Nielson Device mounting interface for your suppressor this will need to be assembled into the suppressor mount as well. Insert the piston (with spring over it) into the mount and lock it down with the piston cap.
steps.cite: BANISH 46-V2 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — INSTALLATION OF SUPPRESSOR DIRECT THREAD AND NIELSON DEVICE, p.4

steps.title: Check the seat before firing and before stripping
steps.action: Confirm the thread mount is fully shouldered on the barrel with no visible gap, and that any crush washer from an earlier muzzle device is gone. On a can rated to .460 an unshouldered mount has a great deal of energy behind it.
steps.prose: The mount is the only thing holding a 15.3 oz can concentric to the bore. A gap at the shoulder is a lever arm.
steps.quote: Check the fit between your barrel and silencer before firing! The thread mount must be fully shouldered on the barrel.
steps.cite: BANISH 46-V2 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: If there is any gap DO NOT fire the host with the silencer attached.

steps.title: Let it cool before you handle it
steps.action: After firing, treat the can as too hot to hold. Banish tells you to use extreme caution and offers a Silencer Central suppressor cover or gloves for retightening a hot can. On a big-bore host the heat arrives quickly even at modest round counts.
steps.prose: The stainless blast baffle at the rear is the hottest part of the assembly and it is right where your hand goes.
steps.quote: When removing the silencer, use extreme caution as it may be hot to the touch after firing.
steps.cite: BANISH 46-V2 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — WARNING, p.2

steps.title: Unthread the Banish 46 off the muzzle
steps.action: Turn the can counter-clockwise off the host. Banish's install instruction is hand tighten only, so removal should be by hand too. Direct-thread and HUB-mounted cans both tighten themselves under fire, which is why the attachment has to be re-checked in use rather than trusted.
steps.prose: Banish's stated interval is after the first 5 discharges and every 30 after that. On a heavy can that is a genuinely useful habit.
steps.caution: Hand tighten only. Do not wrench the can onto the host.
steps.quote: We recommend checking the security of the attachment after 5 discharges of the firearm and every 30 discharges thereafter.
steps.cite: BANISH 46-V2 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — WARNING, p.2

steps.title: Protect the bare threads and never fire an obstructed can
steps.action: Fit a thread protector or muzzle device to the exposed threads for storage and transport, and before the can goes back on, sight through it and confirm the bore is clear. Mud, dirt, a patch or standing solvent all count as obstructions and Banish forbids firing through any of them.
steps.prose: On this can the mount can be removed for cleaning, so check the mount bore as well as the tube — it is a second place for a patch to end up.
steps.quote: Silencers must be free of obstructions such as mud, dirt, etc. DO NOT attempt to shoot through an obstructed silencer.
steps.cite: BANISH 46-V2 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — WARNING, p.2
steps.warn: Sight through the can AND the mount before it goes on.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The Banish 46 is off the host with its mount accounted for — that is the routine strip. The twelve-baffle teardown is the Deep Clean and Banish sets it at every 50 to 100 rounds. It also rules out solid lead or plated lead bullets in this can, which matters more here than on a jacketed-only can because the .460 end of the range is where cast bullets live.
steps.prose: That interval is short, and it is short because the only way into this can is the end cap.
steps.quote: It is recommended that the suppressor be cleaned every 50 - 100 rounds fired. The use of solid lead or plated lead bullets is not recommended.
steps.cite: BANISH 46-V2 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — DISASSEMBLY AND CLEANING, p.6

deepSteps.title: End cap off — tool key and T-45 torx
deepSteps.action: With the can off the host and the host unloaded, fit the supplied tool key with a T-45 torx wrench and unscrew the end cap. Banish recommends bonding the torx and the key together with JB Weld so the two-part tool cannot slip or be separated.
deepSteps.prose: The cap goes back at only 40 in-lbs on this can, so a damaged tool interface will make it impossible to tell a properly seated cap from an over-torqued one.
deepSteps.quote: Using the provided tool key and T-45 torx wrench, remove the end cap of the suppressor. For best results, we recommend permanently attaching the T-45 torx wrench and the tool key together. This can be done with “JB Weld” or similar product found at any local hardware store.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 46-V2 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — DISASSEMBLY AND CLEANING, p.6

deepSteps.title: Front module off the main tube
deepSteps.action: Unthread the front module from the main tube. It is the section that holds the front of the baffle stack, and taking it off is what opens the tube up for the soak.
deepSteps.prose: Keep the module and the main tube identifiable. Their internal baffle counts differ and the stack has to go back in the order it came out.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the front module from the main tube.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 46-V2 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — DISASSEMBLY AND CLEANING, p.6

deepSteps.title: ⛔ The barrel-threaded end cap does not come off the main tube
deepSteps.action: Do not attempt to separate the rear, barrel-threaded end from the main tube. Banish states it is not intended to be removed. That end carries the mount interface and the datum the baffle stack indexes against, and there is no published way to take it off.
deepSteps.prose: Everything you need to clean is reachable from the front once the front cap and module are off.
deepSteps.quote: The end cap of the suppressor that threads onto the barrel is not intended to be removed from the main tube of the suppressor.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 46-V2 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — DISASSEMBLY AND CLEANING, p.6
deepSteps.warn: Rear end of the main tube: not removable.

deepSteps.title: Soak 24 hours, then push the stack out
deepSteps.action: Spray solvent through the inside and leave it a full 24 hours before anything is pushed. Then drive the baffles out with a wooden dowel or Banish's optional Baffle Removal Tool. A dry, carbon-locked stack forced out scores the baffles and the tube wall.
deepSteps.prose: Wooden dowel, never a steel rod. The tube's bore is the reference surface for the whole stack.
deepSteps.caution: Twenty-four hours of soak before any force.
deepSteps.quote: Push baffles out of the tube with our Baffle Removal Tool (sold separately) or a wooden dowel.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 46-V2 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — DISASSEMBLY AND CLEANING, p.6

deepSteps.title: Twelve baffles — eleven indexed and one accuracy baffle
deepSteps.action: This can holds 12 baffles: one accuracy baffle and eleven indexed ones. Identify the accuracy baffle as it comes out and set it aside, because it goes back in one place only. Scrub every baffle and the tube's inside with a stiff brass or nylon brush and solvent or carbon killer, then confirm nothing wet is left in the can.
deepSteps.prose: Banish's own note is that care must be taken when reassembling, and on a twelve-piece indexed stack that is not a formality.
deepSteps.quote: The suppressor has 12 baffles, one accuracy baffle and eleven baffles. Care must be taken when reassembling.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 46-V2 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — DISASSEMBLY AND CLEANING, p.6
deepSteps.warn: Make sure all parts are clean and solvent has been removed.

deepSteps.title: Restack eleven, then the accuracy baffle on top
deepSteps.action: On a flat surface stack the eleven matching baffles on each other with every indexing tab aligned and fully engaged, then set the accuracy baffle on top of them and confirm the index tab from the baffles below is fully engaged in it. Slide the tube over the stack, take it to the edge of the table and push the baffles up with one finger.
deepSteps.prose: The accuracy baffle is the last thing on the stack, not the first. Getting that backwards is the reassembly error this can invites.
deepSteps.quote: Stack accuracy baffle on top of the eleven baffles. Make sure the index tab from the baffles is fully engaged in the accuracy baffle.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 46-V2 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — ASSEMBLY, p.7

deepSteps.title: ⛔ End cap to 40 in-lbs — NOT 110-120
deepSteps.action: Flip the assembly open end up, apply anti-seize to the threads and start the end cap. Tighten lightly and check the tell: with the baffles aligned only the 45 degree bevel shows, about 1/32 of an inch. Then finish at 40 in-lbs — a third of the figure Banish uses on the 30, the 223 and the Gold.
deepSteps.prose: Carrying 110-120 in-lbs across from a sibling Banish book to this can is the single most damaging mistake available here, and the books sit next to each other on the same website.
deepSteps.quote: Finish tightening end cap to 40 in-lbs.
deepSteps.cite: BANISH 46-V2 — OWNER'S MANUAL — NOT PRINTED — ASSEMBLY, p.7
deepSteps.warn: 40 in-lbs. Read it off THIS manual and no other.

cleaning.name: BAFFLE STACK
tasks: Soak the interior with solvent for 24 hours before pushing anything out
Push the stack out with a wooden dowel or the Baffle Removal Tool
Identify the single accuracy baffle and keep it separate from the eleven indexed baffles
Scrub every baffle and the tube interior with a stiff brass or nylon brush
Confirm all solvent has been removed before reassembly

cleaning.name: END CAP
tasks: Apply anti-seize to the threads before fitting
Use the tool key with a T-45 torx wrench
Check only the 45 degree bevel shows, about 1/32 inch, before torquing
Finish at 40 in-lbs — NOT the 110-120 in-lbs used on other Banish rifle cans

cleaning.name: HUB MOUNT
tasks: Thread the mount into the suppressor and tighten to 50-60 in-lbs before the can goes on a host
For a Nielson device, build the piston and spring into the mount and lock it with the piston cap
Check the mount bore for obstructions along with the tube
Re-check the can's attachment after 5 discharges and every 30 thereafter

cleaning.name: SCHEDULE AND AMMUNITION
tasks: Do not use solid lead or plated lead bullets in this can

reassembly: Stack the eleven matching baffles with every indexing tab aligned and fully engaged.
Set the accuracy baffle on top and confirm the index tab from the baffles below is engaged in it.
Slide the tube over the stack, take it to the edge of the table and push the baffles up the tube with one finger.
Flip the assembly open end up and apply anti-seize to the threads before the end cap goes on.
Tighten the cap lightly and confirm only the 45 degree bevel shows at about 1/32 inch.
Finish tightening the end cap to 40 in-lbs — not the 110-120 in-lbs used on other Banish rifle cans.
Thread the mount into the suppressor at 50-60 in-lbs, then fit the can to the host hand tight with no gap at the shoulder.
fncheck: After rebuilding, check the end cap shows only its 45 degree bevel at about 1/32 inch — more than that means the twelve-baffle stack is not indexed. Confirm the cap was torqued to 40 in-lbs and not to a figure borrowed from another Banish book. Sight through the can and the mount for one clear channel with no standing solvent, then confirm the mount is fully shouldered on the barrel with no visible gap.
